subject.title: [Bug]: Codex app-server session wedges indefinitely after a 429 rate-limit burst — terminal-idle watchdog still gated by `activeAppServerTurnRequests > 0` (regression/incomplete fix of #82681)

question: Is current-main source and test proof enough to close this issue now, or should it stay open until a post-PR-102160 build is live-confirmed against a 429 burst?
rationale: The implementation evidence points to a structural fix, but the latest human status comment explicitly asks for live confirmation on a release containing the lifecycle stack and the latest stable release does not contain it.

options.title: Keep Open For Live Confirmation
options.body: Leave this issue open until a release or test build containing PR 102160 has journald/live-run evidence that shared Codex app-server sessions recover after a 429-silent wedge.

options.title: Close As Main-Only Implemented
options.body: Close now using current-main source and test proof, asking for a new issue or reopen evidence if a post-fix build still wedges past the completion-idle window.

recommendation.title: Keep Open For Live Confirmation
recommendation.body: Leave this issue open until a release or test build containing PR 102160 has journald/live-run evidence that shared Codex app-server sessions recover after a 429-silent wedge.

likelyOwner.reason: Authored the merged lifecycle/Codex liveness stack and posted the current keep-open-until-live-confirmation status.
